column2: req_desc

Reserve from live availability
A parent reserves an instrument type and size for their own child, and the server assigns the available serial that sorts first and places a hold, as qualified in Business rules.

One winner for the last unit
When several reservations race for the last available unit of a type and size, exactly one succeeds and every other gets the unavailable answer with alternatives, and no serial is ever on two open contracts.

Delivery day by store cutoff
Each reservation's delivery day is its school's next delivery day whose cutoff in the store's time zone is later than the server's clock when the reservation arrives, whatever the device clock or zone says.

Reserving from the size picker
A parent picks a child, instrument and size with keyboard or pointer, reserves, and sees the serial, hold deadline and delivery day, or the unavailable message with alternatives they can choose straight away.

Send the signing link
The store owner sends a signing link for a reserved contract, the parent receives it by email, and sending again replaces the earlier link.

Signing link limits
A signing link opens only its own agreement and stops working once signed, after its lifetime, when its hold expires, when revoked, or when replaced.

Sign and store the agreement
Signing through a live link stores the signed agreement PDF in object storage, binds the contract to the price list in force that day and moves it to signed, or changes nothing when storage is unreachable.

Signing by keyboard
A parent can read, fill and sign the agreement page using only the keyboard, with visible focus and the outcome announced.

Activate exactly once with the stored agreement
The store owner activates a signed contract only when its signed PDF is in object storage, and however many activation requests arrive at once exactly one succeeds, with one Kill Bill account, one monthly subscription and one history entry.

Monthly invoice in exact cents
Each contract's monthly invoice lists its signed base rent, the optional waiver and sales tax at the rate in force on its billing date, in exact cents with the published rounding rule.

Payments reach Kill Bill before equity
A recorded payment becomes a Kill Bill purchase on the contract's account before any equity is credited, and a receipt email follows.

Exact payment split
Every payment is split into base rent, waiver and tax by the published rule at the tax rate in force on the day it is charged, and the three parts always add up to the amount charged.

Payment retries are safe
Repeating a payment with the same idempotency key, including several copies sent at once, gives one Kill Bill charge, one ledger entry and one receipt with every copy getting the first answer, and reusing a key with a different amount is rejected.

Simultaneous money actions never overshoot
Simultaneous money and state actions on one contract are taken one at a time, so equity never passes the purchase price and a payment that would pass it is refused before any Kill Bill charge.

Recording a payment from the contract sheet
The store owner records a payment in a dialog and sees the split, the new equity and the receipt notice on the contract sheet.

Size exchange moves equity in a pair
Exchanging an active violin or cello for a larger size closes the old contract and opens exactly one successor with a paired debit and credit that conserve total equity, even when the request arrives several times at once with one idempotency key.

Exchanging a size from the contract sheet
The store owner picks the new size in a dialog and lands on the successor contract showing the carried equity.

Payoff quote for any month
The server quotes equity, discount tier, payoff, sales tax and total for any month from 0 to the term length of a signed or active contract.

All-or-nothing buyout
A buyout charges the current payoff plus sales tax in Kill Bill, closes the contract as owned, closes its equity ledger and queues the ownership letter, or does none of these, as qualified in Business rules.

Buyout Rail
The contract sheet's rail moves one month per step by drag, tap or keys, fills the instrument model's brass band and the equity gauge in proportion to equity, swaps the tier label and shows the server's payoff for that month.

Buyout Rail with reduced motion
With reduced motion requested, the rail is a plain range slider beside a month-by-month table and every value changes without animation.

Buying out from the rail
A parent or the owner confirms a buyout for the payoff plus tax from the contract sheet and sees the contract turn owned.

Effective-dated price lists
The store owner publishes a price list with rents, sales tax rate and discount schedule effective today or later, and the version in force on any date follows the published rule.

Contracts keep their signed terms
Every surface of a signed contract uses the rent, waiver, purchase price, term and tiers it was signed under, while sales tax follows the rate in force on the billing date or the day charged, as qualified in Business rules.

Withdrawing a scheduled price list
The store owner can withdraw a price list only while its effective date is later than the store's today, and afterwards the version in force on every date and every unsigned reservation's terms are exactly what they were before it was published.

Managing price lists on screen
The store owner fills in the new price list form, sees every version labelled with its standing, and withdraws a scheduled one after confirming.

Fleet and student intake
The store owner adds serialized instruments and students, and the numbered fleet register lists every instrument with its status.

Director roster limited to school and fields
A band director sees only their own school's roster, with only the published student, instrument and delivery fields.

Roster summary equals its rows
The roster's count of students per delivery status always equals the tally of its rows at request time, including holds that lapsed on their own and size exchanges.

Roster CSV export
The roster CSV export holds the same rows as the roster and neutralises any cell beginning with a formula character.

Checking the roster before delivery day
A band director signs in, sees the roster summary and each student's instrument and delivery status as a word with its own icon in text meeting 4.5:1 contrast, and downloads the CSV.

Delivery days across daylight saving
Each school lists its next four delivery days, each with its cutoff at the same store wall-clock time on the day before, including across a daylight-saving change, and a delivery day leaves the list at its exact cutoff instant.

Delivery-day notice
The store owner sends a school's band director an email for one of its upcoming delivery days, listing only the students, instruments and serials on that day's manifest.

Condition photos judged by content
Condition photos are accepted only as JPEG, PNG or WebP images within the published limits, judged by their content, then re-encoded and stored under server-chosen names.

Condition upload is all or nothing
A condition check stores its event and every photo together or nothing at all, so a contract's stored condition photos always equal the photos of its recorded checks.

Recording condition at the counter
The repair tech records a check-out, exchange or return condition check with photos and sees it in the contract's condition history.

Families reach only their own contracts
A parent can reach contracts, statements, quotes, invoices, photos, agreements and bills of sale only for their own children, and any other ID answers 404.

Family totals stay with the family
My family's totals are computed at request time from the parent's own children only, follow lapsed holds, payoffs and reversals, and stay unchanged by other families' activity and by the family's own size exchanges.

Family overview
A parent sees each child with their contracts, equity and status, plus the family totals, and can reach reservation and the contract sheet from there.

Equity statement equals its ledger
A contract's equity always equals the sum of its ledger entries, which are never edited or deleted, and corrections are new reversal entries.

Contract state machine
Contracts move only along the published states, and every other move answers 409 with the instrument, ledger and history unchanged.

Unsigned holds expire
A reservation not signed by its hold deadline counts as expired from that deadline on every surface and releases its instrument, with no request needed to trigger it.

Attributed contract history
Every contract state move appends exactly one history entry naming its actor and time, a lapsed hold is recorded once by the system at its exact deadline, and rejected moves record nothing.

Sign-in and roles
Seeded staff, parents and directors sign in with email and password, and each endpoint is open only to the roles the API lists.

One error order and shape
Every error uses one JSON shape and the API applies one published precedence order.

Billing and storage outages
When Kill Bill or object storage is unreachable, every action that needs it answers 503 with nothing changed in any system and the screen says so, as qualified in Services.

Controlled server clock
When BELLROLL_CLOCK_START is set, every server time rule, including the store's today, reads one clock that starts at that instant when the app starts and advances in real time.

Run manifest and health
The app installs, builds and serves from its run manifest on the published port and answers the health check.

Server boundary
The server enforces same-origin requests and body limits and never serves source files or credentials.

Layout at three viewports
Every screen fits 375 by 812, 768 by 1024 and 1280 by 800 without horizontal scrolling, with tap targets at least 44 pixels.

Keyboard and visible focus
Every action works from the keyboard with a visible focus ring, and dialogs keep Tab inside, close on Escape and return focus to their opener.

Motion vocabulary
Motion uses the three published speeds, has no unnamed looping decoration, and stops entirely when reduced motion is requested.

Catalogued register look
Screens read as a numbered museum register on cream paper, with ink text, hairline rules, a single brass accent reserved for equity and ownership, and procedural instrument models drawn in ink.

Credentials from environment
Every service URL and credential is read from the environment at start and never hard-coded or sent to the browser.

Payment reversals
The store owner reverses a recorded payment on an active contract with one Kill Bill refund on the original payment and one reversal ledger entry of exactly its stored base part, at most once per payment, with retries handled like payments.

Reversing a payment from the contract sheet
The store owner reverses a payment from the equity ledger in a dialog with a reason and sees the payment marked reversed, the reduced equity and the refreshed Buyout Rail.

Bill of sale at payoff
Every move to paid off stores a bill of sale PDF that the owner and the family can download, so the bill of sale exists exactly when the contract is paid off and a refused payoff leaves no object and no new Kill Bill transaction, and a failed payoff leaves no object, while a Kill Bill charge it had already confirmed stays and is adopted on retry.

Billing anniversary dates
Each active contract's billing dates are its activation store date plus whole months with the day clamped to month end, each computed from the anchor, and a size-exchange successor keeps its predecessor's anchor.

Exact starting state
However many app instances start at once against one database, schema and seed are applied exactly once and new contract IDs come from one sequence starting at C-1004 without collisions.

Live size availability on Reserve
While the Reserve page is open, its size counts follow the server within 6 seconds without a reload, keeping the parent's choices and focus, and a selected size that runs out moves to the first available size of that instrument in size order with the published announcement.

Delivery line follows the server's cutoff
The Reserve page's delivery line switches to the next delivery day within 2 seconds after the chosen school's cutoff passes on the server's clock, whatever the device clock or zone says.

Signing page expires in place
An open signing page shows its link expiry and replaces the signing form with the expired message within 2 seconds after the link expires on the server's clock, whatever the device clock says.

Exact width bands
Layout changes only at the published width bands, and the roster and fleet register show exactly the published columns in each band, with hidden columns absent from the page and the accessibility tree.

Delivery-day picker survives its cutoff
When a listed delivery day's cutoff passes with the Schools page open, that school's delivery days refresh in place within 2 seconds, still-valid selections stay, and a passed selection is cleared with the published message.

Refused photo named and batch kept
When one photo in a condition batch is refused, the API names its position, and the dialog names the file, keeps every chosen photo and moves focus to that photo's Remove button.

Return to the requested page after sign-in
A signed-out visitor to a signed-in page lands back on that exact page and query after signing in when it is a same-site path open to their role, and otherwise on their role's home.

Closing confirmed by Kill Bill
Return, write-off, exchange and payoff commit only after Kill Bill reads the contract's subscription back as cancelled, and otherwise answer 503 with nothing changed in Bellroll.

Adopting an interrupted Kill Bill transaction
Before any charge or refund the server looks up its published external key in Kill Bill and adopts a successful transaction of the same amount instead of charging again, while a different amount is refused with nothing written.

Buyout Rail by touch
On a phone, a horizontal finger drag or a tap on a notch moves the rail month by month, a vertical swipe over the rail scrolls the page and leaves the month unchanged, and the handle is at least 44 by 44 pixels.

Collapsed menu is unavailable
In the narrow band the main navigation sits behind a Menu button, and while collapsed its links are neither reachable by Tab nor present in the accessibility tree.

Form errors on their fields
A refused price list, instrument or student form reports every invalid field at once, each message is tied to its field, and focus moves to the first invalid field.

Motion choreography
The rail handle settles with a measured spring, dialogs rise in and leave on time, the register row grows into the contract header, and figures roll to their exact values, each within its published speed and instant under reduced motion.

Turnable 3D instrument model
The contract sheet shows a WebGL model of the instrument with a brass band at the equity fraction, which drag and arrow keys turn in published steps, which never moves at idle, and which falls back to the flat drawing without WebGL.

Motion and 3D libraries
The browser animates with the Motion library and draws the instrument model with three.js, with no other animation or 3D engine.
/app/run.json holds exactly string install, build and serve commands plus "_schema":"run-manifest-v1".
/app/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md lists every shipped package (the production dependency tree from npm ls --omit=dev --all --json) and every bundled font, each with its licence.

Shipped packages (the production dependency tree from npm ls --omit=dev --all --json) and fonts use only the MIT, ISC, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, Apache-2.0, 0BSD, BlueOak-1.0.0 or SIL OFL 1.1 licences.
No datastore beyond Postgres, Kill Bill, MinIO and Mailpit: no SQLite, Redis, embedded databases or files used as storage.
The provided service configuration and its credentials stay untouched, and the app reaches services only through the published environment variables.
Application source is TypeScript, with no hand-written JavaScript source outside generated build output and tool configuration files.
The browser loads nothing from another origin. Fonts, icons, the motion and 3D libraries and every script are bundled and served by the app.
